This is Voice Harness: a local prototype workspace for evaluating and assuring voice AI. The idea is simple. Configure the test. Inspect what happened. And compare the evidence.

Everything starts with the runs. Filter by scenario, provider, outcome, status and time, then open any run to see exactly what was recorded. This is a snapshot of the latest fifty, not an overall success rate.
Each evaluation can be shaped to your question. Choose the scenario, the audio condition and the prompt profile. Set a seed so a fixture can be repeated, and decide whether to retain the audio.
The caller is part of the test. Pick a persona and a voice, then bound the number of turns and the length of the call. This live caller is still a pilot, so its fidelity needs review.

The scenario library defines the challenge. Explore the expected behaviour, the tool calls and the criteria, and filter by customer group, locale and audio condition. The scenarios are synthetic banking journeys, and the expectations are always explicit.

The catalogue can grow. Download a scenario definition, edit it, and validate it through the import dialog to store a new version. Importing saves the definition. Running it still needs a registered runner.

To compare providers, design a bake-off. Choose the providers, the scenario groups, the prompt profile and how many times to repeat each test. The launch flow shows the setup and billing requirements up front. Nothing was launched for this tour.

Not every team weighs quality the same way. Adjust the priorities and watch the report respond. These custom weights are exploratory, they never overwrite the stored assessment, and they don't establish a statistically significant winner.

Then open the evidence. Inspect the gates and the scorecards, download the report, or take the observations as C S V or J S O N. You can also clone the configuration to run it again. This batch covers six hundred settled runs, with no clear winner.

Compare two runs side by side. Read both conversations together, with the metric differences, the transcript revisions, and separate verdicts for the model and the platform. Differences here don't amount to a provider ranking.

When a run fails, see where. Follow the recorded system activity, including denied tools, policy decisions and released audio. In this example the model failed but the platform passed, because enforcement and behaviour are measured separately.
Reviews stay traceable. Rerun or assess an existing run, preserve its evidence, and export a signed evidence bundle. These controls are shown here only. Nothing was changed for the tour.

You can also try the journey yourself. Choose a happy or a challenge path, use voice or text input, and set whether assessment happens before or after playback. Human-driven sessions use live providers, so they do incur usage.

The telephone pilot customises a demo call. Edit the goal, the supplied details and the delivery style, and choose generated or fixed responses with gated or native speech. It is a bounded diagnostic for authorised demo lines, not independent platform verification.

Findings and holds keep the evidence safe. Review the assurance findings and manage preservation holds, so retained evidence stays available until a hold expires. A hold can't restore evidence that has already been purged.

Before anything runs, check readiness. Provider coverage separates verified support from the current server configuration. On this captured server, six provider families are verified but none are ready, so the setup gaps stay visible rather than hidden.

Keep an eye on spend. Review provider balances, dated manual readings and warning thresholds before starting another evaluation. Saved balances are historical observations, and provider reporting can lag.

The workspace is yours to set up. Use the light, dark or automatic theme, and move between evaluations, reports and operational controls in the browser. The interface and evidence are local, though live calls still use your configured cloud services.

So: a working prototype today, and evidence for the next decision. The next step is to apply the same journeys to your actual Connect or third party configuration, and then validate the end to end customer experience. These tests don't benchmark Amazon Connect.
